**Affine cellular algebras and asymptotic algebras**

*PAULA A.A.B. CARVALHO, STEFFEN KOENIG, AND CHRISTIAN LOMP*

32 pp, 11 sections.

**Abstract.** The theory of affine cellular algebras A is extended to incorporate their asymptotic algebras ˆA, clarifying unexpected differences between classical and affine situations and comparing with Lusztig’s asymptotic Hecke algebras. The main new results are about a double centraliser property between A and ˆA, about constructing ˆA from cell modules of A, about existence of an embedding A →ˆA and about a faithful functor from torsionless ˆA-modules to A-modules as well as about the embedding being weakly spectrum preserving (in the sense of Baum and Nistor) and about non-zero endomorphisms of cell modules being injective, while there are no non-zero homomorphisms between non-isomorphic cell modules.

**Outline.** Front matter; 1 Introduction; 2 Determinants for affine Cellular Algebras; 3 Homomorphisms between affine cell ideals.; 4 The asymptotic algebra of an affine cellular; 5 Properties of the embedding into the asympto; 6 Examples and methods; 6.1 An explicit example; 6.2 Extended affine Hecke algebra of type A; 6.3 Gram determinants and Jucys Murphy element; References
